analysis.title: Central Bank Watcher November 2026
key_insights: Central scenario: the Fed and ECB each deliver at least one more hike in Q1 2027 before a temporary policy rate peak, assuming energy prices stay elevated amid the Middle East conflict. All three of the Fed, ECB and BoJ look set to hike after December, having paused in October.

An earlier peak in US and euro-area rates, potentially after a December hike, cannot be ruled out but would likely require a major risk-off move across equity and credit markets. Both the Fed and ECB are increasingly focused on broader financial conditions.

A sharp tightening in financial conditions, from a bond yield surge or a steep equity sell-off (not merely an AI rotation), could do part of the central banks' tightening work for them. For the ECB, a drastic further deterioration in French government bonds could be enough to trigger a pause.

Fed held at 3.75-4.00% in October after a 25 bps hike in September. Governors Cook and Hammack dissented in favor of another 25 bps hike. Statement changes were minimal, with the economy expanding 'at a strong pace' and inflation 'elevated'. Robeco reads the closing language as a subtle hint that tightening could resume in December.

Chair Warsh kept forward guidance minimal but said financing and credit conditions had begun to tighten for some businesses and households. This tempered market expectations for 2027 hikes, a year with seven meetings instead of eight.

Robeco expects a December Fed hike plus one more 25 bps hike in Q1 2027, which would fully reverse the three cuts delivered in 2H 2025. Risks are skewed toward more than 50 bps of tightening over six months. Robeco disagrees with the higher-for-longer path priced by markets and expects easing to resume in late 2027/early 2028.
Fed scenario probabilities: central 50%, higher for longer 35%, mild 2027 recession 15%. The probability-weighted funds rate path falls below market pricing from 2H 2027.

Robeco assumes the 10-year Treasury yield peak is not yet in, since peaks typically come around the second-to-last hike and the Fed usually keeps hiking until M2 growth (5.7% YoY) slows meaningfully. The yield curve is expected to flatten further despite the recent re-steepening.

ECB held rates in October. Energy prices and tighter financial conditions dominated the meeting. Indirect and second-round (wage) effects from energy have been limited so far, but the risk rises the longer energy prices stay high.

French OAT spreads have jumped on budget negotiations and next year's presidential elections, dragging lower-rated euro government bonds with them. Italian 10-year BTP yields are near 4.5%, up 100 bps since early July, which reduces the urgency for further ECB tightening.

Brent is back at its early-March highs, refinery margins have jumped and TTF gas is up 70% from its March peak. ECB staff energy scenarios have moved above the 'adverse' scenario. Robeco sees 4% HICP inflation by year end.

Robeco's ECB base case is a 25 bps hike in December and another in March, taking the deposit rate to 3.00%. It doubts the euro-area economy can sustain a deposit rate above 2.5% for long and expects a flatter yield curve. Further hikes may be skipped if OAT spreads widen materially and spill over.

Lagarde pointed to the TPI as an available tool for disorderly bond moves without specifics. Robeco thinks spreads would need to jump much further before the ECB uses it. Lagarde's departure is due in February.

PBoC has not cut its 7-day reverse repo rate this year, likely due to bank net interest margin concerns and a desire to keep some CNY appreciation. It narrowed the rate corridor from 70bp to 50bp and cut rates on structural facilities.

PBoC is shifting its main policy rate to the overnight reverse repo rate, currently 1.25%. DR001 had slipped below the 7-day rate, which Robeco reads as de facto easing. Money market conditions are expected to stay very loose, pointing to a prolonged policy pause.

China Q3 GDP beat expectations but growth is uneven and driven by external demand. PPI is up 5% YoY, signaling deflation pressure has receded for now. The equity market is about 20% below its end-June level.

CGB 5-year and 10-year yields are nearing the late-2024 lows. Robeco sees limited further downside, especially at the long end. Momentum could push the 30-year below 2%, but the PBoC warned of bond bubble risks when it hit 1.80% in January 2025, which marked a turning point.

BoJ voted 8-1 to hold at 1.25% in October. It said underlying CPI is generally consistent with the 2% target and raised growth and inflation forecasts, with core ex fresh food and energy above target through 2028. Ueda said every meeting is live and rates are below neutral.
BoJ equity portfolio unwind was accelerated, now set to take 43 years instead of 112, with a very small expected market impact.

Robeco sees BoJ core inflation rising to a peak around Q1 2027, with wage demands above 2% for over three years, positive real wages, services inflation broadening and Tankan showing firms see conditions as accommodative. Rates are not yet restrictive.
Robeco's BoJ base case is quarterly hikes to 2% over 12 months, with risks tilted toward a faster pace. Robeco stays modestly short front-end Japanese rates.

FX-hedged JGB yields are above Bunds and Treasuries, drawing global rate-sensitive buyers. Recent flow data show more domestic buyers in the long end, making Robeco more optimistic about long-end flattening exposure on yield spikes.

trade_ideas.rationale: Inflation is likely to pick up and Robeco expects pressure on the BoJ to signal a faster return toward neutral than priced.

trade_ideas.description: Long-end JGB flattening exposure on yield spikes

trade_ideas.description: Yield curve flattening in the US and euro area
trade_ideas.rationale: The 10-year Treasury peak is not yet in, and the ECB is unlikely to sustain a deposit rate above 2.5% for long.
trade_ideas.risk: Risk assets falling sharply so that the December hike is the last, or a mild 2027 recession.

risk_factors: Renewed escalation in the Middle East would keep energy prices and inflation elevated.
A sharp tightening in financial conditions from a bond yield surge or steep equity sell-off could end the hiking cycle early.
A mild US recession in 2027, assigned 15% probability.
Further deterioration in French OAT spreads spilling over to other euro government bonds.
Energy price pass-through to wages and broader price setting in the euro area.
A PBoC warning about bond market bubble risks if the 30-year CGB yield falls below 2%.
Chinese equities about 20% below the end-June level.
charts_described: Figure 1 plots the GS Financial Conditions Index for the US, Eurozone and Japan, where 100 marks country-specific long-term averages and values above 100 indicate looser than average conditions.
Figure 2 plots the Fed funds upper bound through Q1 2028 with a central scenario (50%), higher for longer (35%) and a mild 2027 recession (15%), plus a probability-weighted average path.
Figure 4 shows the gap between 10y CGB yields and short-term money market rates has narrowed a lot.
vol_and_positioning: Robeco stays modestly short front-end Japanese rates.
Robeco is more optimistic about adding long-end JGB flattening exposure if yields spike, since domestic buyers are increasing exposure.

Global investors added long-end JGB exposure for four years because FX-hedged JGB yields exceed Bunds and Treasuries. These buyers are rate sensitive and opportunistic, causing volatility in sell-offs.
geopolitical: Lingering conflict in the Middle East with a risk of renewed escalation keeps energy prices elevated.
French budget negotiations and next year's French presidential elections are widening OAT spreads.
Lagarde's earlier-than-scheduled departure from the ECB presidency, due in February, was raised at the press conference.
Fed rate decisions are being made shortly before the US midterm elections.
cross_bank_references: Robeco cites Goldman Sachs for the financial conditions index in Figure 1.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price higher-for-longer, with the funds rate near 4.50% to 4.55% through September 2027. Tough rhetoric and two hawkish dissents support further hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: Robeco expects inflation risks to recede and growth risks to re-emerge, with easing resuming by late 2027/early 2028. Credit and financing conditions are already tightening for some businesses and households.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp fall in risk assets, which would make the December hike the last and bring Robeco's 15% mild 2027 recession scenario into play.

tension_points.bull_case: Energy prices at early-March Brent highs, TTF up 70% and 4% HICP by year end support hikes in December and March.
tension_points.bear_case: Widening OAT spreads and Italian BTP yields near 4.5% tighten financial conditions on their own and reduce the urgency to hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If OAT spreads continue to widen materially and spill over to other markets, additional ECB hikes may be skipped.
